name: WPA Code of Ethics for Psychiatry
editionLabel: Adopted by the WPA General Assembly in October 2020 (supersedes the Declaration of Madrid)
summary: The World Psychiatric Association's code is a global ethics statement for psychiatrists. It was adopted by the WPA General Assembly in October 2020, supersedes the Declaration of Madrid, and has four parts: ethics in clinical practice, in psychiatric education, in research and in public mental health. WPA describes it as a living document to be updated as psychiatry changes. National psychiatric associations' codes and national law govern individual practice. This is a summary in the app's own words. It is information, not legal advice.

keyReminders.text: Respect the person's dignity, autonomy and values, and involve them, and with consent their family, in treatment decisions.
Use involuntary treatment only when the law allows and less restrictive options will not keep the person or others safe, and review it often.
Protect confidentiality and explain its legal limits; share information only as needed for care or as the law requires.
Consider culture and social context in diagnosis and care, and oppose discrimination and stigma against people with mental illness.

regulatorNote: Psychiatrists are licensed nationally or by state or province, and national psychiatric associations have their own codes. Local law and the local regulator take precedence.

verification.note: The October 2020 adoption, four-part structure and supersession of the Declaration of Madrid were confirmed through search results indexing wpanet.org and a World Psychiatry article on PubMed Central (PMC8129851). A person must load the official page before release.
